overview: Saint-Jérôme had 80,213 residents in the 2021 Census, up 7.9 percent from 2016, nearly double the Quebec average. The city covers 90.18 square kilometres at the gateway to the Laurentians, combining a historic downtown with newer neighbourhoods in Bellefeuille, Lafontaine and Saint-Antoine.

As the regional seat, it draws people for health care, government services and shopping, and the city is opening large tracts of land for industry. For a local business, that means customers from across the region, steady growth in new households, and rising demand from manufacturers and their workers.
